plan: [ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values and rational opponents, bidding one’s true value is a weakly dominant strategy. It maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks paying more than my value if others bid high; underbidding risks losing when winning would yield positive surplus. With three bidders, payment equals the second-highest bid if I win, so truthful bidding preserves all profitable wins without extra cost. Therefore, I will bid my value exactly: $23. ]

[ Single round, independent private values, second-price (Vickrey) auction with three bidders. Truthful bidding is a dominant strategy: bidding my value maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks winning when the second-highest bid exceeds my value (negative surplus). Underbidding risks losing when the second-highest bid is below my value (missed positive surplus). No history to leverage; no signaling benefits. Therefore, bid exactly my value: 18.0. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid exactly my value: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies or beliefs. Underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable; overbidding risks winning at a price above my value if others overbid or have values between my value and my inflated bid. With value $39 and 0.1 increments allowed, I bid 39. ]
